task: Task 3 — Keyboard Selection Edge Cases and Accessibility Contract Reconciliation
scope: Characterization only. No production change. Genuine trusted keyboard input via Playwright; assertions read public-observable DOM (combobox aria-*, aria-activedescendant resolution, option aria-selected, rendered option DOM order) and public `select`/`change` events plus `onSelect`/`onChange` callbacks. Unusual selection semantics are recorded as deviation/observation candidates, NOT normalized to a presumed WAI-ARIA model, and NOT repaired.
t3Note: Task 3 extends the accepted Task-2 real-Chromium harness to keyboard *selection* edges: range selection (Shift+Arrow, Shift+Home/End, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift), Select-All (Ctrl/Cmd+A), selected-first ordering, disabled-in-range, maxSelections, and the ARIA + event chronology of range interactions. Two notable observations are raised as new deviation/observation candidates: P1.3-D05 (Shift+Home/End selects only the boundary endpoint, not the contiguous range) and P1.3-D06 (selectedOptions.placement='selected-first' does not reorder the rendered option list or keyboard navigation, which remain registry order).

T3-00.title: Browser harness (version certification)
findings: Chromium engine version reported 156.0.8078.4 and enforced to equal the recorded build for certification; override runs are flagged.

T3-01.title: Shift+Arrow range selection
findings: An empty multi combobox opens with NO active option; the first Shift+ArrowDown selects the landing option 'a' (anchor = landing), setting active to 'a'.
Each subsequent Shift+ArrowDown/Up extends the contiguous range by one and fills it (a -> a,b -> a,b,c).
Shift+Up extends upward from the current active.
Plain (non-Shift) Arrow moves the active option WITHOUT changing the selection.
Selection is reported in ascending registry order in selectedValues.

T3-02.title: Shift+Home / Shift+End boundary semantics
findings: Shift+End from active 'b' moves active to 'f' and selects ONLY ['f'] — it does NOT select the contiguous range a..f.
Shift+Home from active 'b' moves active to 'a' and selects ONLY ['a'] — it does NOT select the range a..b.
Shift+Home then Shift+End reports ['a'] then ['f'] (each boundary is endpoint-only; each replaces the prior).
Recorded as P1.3-D05 (endpoint-only boundary range). This differs from a typical spreadsheet-style 'extend to boundary' range. Characterized, not repaired.

T3-03.title: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift additive range
findings: Ctrl+Shift+ArrowDown extends the range additively and preserves prior members: [a] -> a,b -> a,b,c.
Meta (Cmd)+Shift+ArrowDown behaves identically (additive).
Plain Shift (without Ctrl/Cmd) REPLACES a pre-existing selection (clear=on): existing {e}, shift from 'f' yields ['f'].

T3-04.title: Ctrl/Cmd+A select-all payload
findings: Ctrl+A selects all and emits ONLY a `change` event (no `select`) with selectedValues [a..f] and selectedIndices [0,1,2,3,4,5] in registry order.
Cmd (Meta)+A selects all identically.
Ctrl+A is ignored in single mode (selection unchanged).

T3-05.title: selected-first projection ordering
findings: With selectedOptions.placement='selected-first' and a prior selection {e,c}, the rendered option DOM order remains registry order ['a','b','c','d','e','f'] — NOT reordered selected-first.
Keyboard navigation follows registry order: open lands on 'c' (first selected in registry order), ArrowDown -> 'd' -> 'e'.
placement='original' behaves identically (registry order + registry navigation) — baseline comparison.
Recorded as P1.3-D06: the selected-first projection does not manifest as a DOM reorder or a navigation reorder at this configuration. Characterized, not repaired.

T3-06.title: disabled options in ranges
findings: Default disabledOptionBehavior (selectable:false): a disabled option is skipped in the range fill. Range from 'a' moving to 'c' with disabled 'b' yields ['a','c'] (b excluded), active lands 'c'.
disabledOptionBehavior.selectable=true: the disabled option becomes a range member (['a','b']).

T3-07.title: maxSelections during keyboard range
findings: With maxSelections=2, a Shift range clamps at the cap: building a,b then extending further (Shift+ArrowDown, Shift+End) keeps ['a','b'].

T3-08.title: ARIA chronology during range selection
findings: aria-expanded stays 'true' throughout a range; aria-activedescendant tracks the moving endpoint and changes across each Shift step; the popup stays open (host data-open present).
After a range a..b, option elements 'a' and 'b' expose aria-selected='true' and 'c' exposes 'false'.

T3-09.title: event chronology during keyboard range
findings: Each Shift extension emits, in order: `select` (detail = moving endpoint record, selected=true, multi=true) -> `change` -> `onChange` -> `onSelect`. (The range path emits `select` first, then _emitChange fires `change`+`onChange`, then the handler invokes `onSelect` last.)
A range does NOT emit `open`/`close`; the popup stays open across the range.

T3-10.title: harness integrity
findings: A full keyboard range flow (open empty multi, build a..d via four Shift+ArrowDown) drives state via public surface only: getSelectedValues()==[a,b,c,d], active 'd', popup open.

P1.3-D05.title: Shift+Home / Shift+End selects only the boundary endpoint
P1.3-D05.meaning: Shift+Home/End move the active option to the first/last selectable option and select ONLY that endpoint, not the contiguous range from the anchor to the boundary. This differs from spreadsheet-style 'extend-to-boundary' range selection. Characterized, not repaired; design decision deferred.

P1.3-D06.title: selectedOptions.placement='selected-first' does not reorder DOM or navigation
P1.3-D06.meaning: At this configuration, selected-first placement does not manifest as a DOM option reorder nor a keyboard navigation reorder; both follow registry order. Characterized, not repaired; design intent to be confirmed before W1-P1 closure.

coverageImplications: Keyboard range/selection edge paths for the P1.3-owned selection surface are now characterized in real Chromium. The traceability matrix (112 records) is unchanged — no record is upgraded to `Existing` without full path coverage. P1.3-D05/D06 are recorded as observations pending Technical Lead disposition.
